- HARDENING_SUGGESTION (not a finding; all lenses NONE) scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh | Location: _pr_probe_repo_init, the `_PR_PROBE_REPO_SLUG` override handling around line ~2165 | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
  PROBLEM: The override slug goes into the origin URL after only the `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$` regex check, and that regex accepts `..` segments and a segment that starts with a dot. So a caller-controlled `_PR_PROBE_REPO_SLUG` such as `../foo` passes the check and ends up in `remote add origin "${server%/}/${probe_repo}.git"`.
  WHY: The reviewer says this is not exploitable today, because the train caller always passes `MT_REPO`, which is already validated as `owner/repo`. The override is still part of the library API, so a future caller could pass a malformed slug. Suggested fix: tighten the regex to `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)*/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)*$`, or check each `/` component on its own (~2 lines).
